questions.question: What HTTP basics does a Rails API developer need?
questions.title: HTTP Basics for Rails APIs
questions.direct_answer: HTTP is request/response: a client sends a request (method + URL + headers + optional body), the server returns a response (status code + headers + body). Methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update; PATCH partial), DELETE (remove). Headers carry metadata (Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer). Status codes: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 4xx client error (400, 401, 403, 404, 422), 5xx server error (500). The body for an API is usually JSON. Stateless: each request carries what it needs (the token in the header); the server keeps no session between requests. Idempotence: GET and DELETE are safe to retry; POST is not.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the request/response model, the verbs, status code families (2xx/4xx/5xx), and that an API body is usually JSON.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Returning 200 for a create (use 201), or forgetting the Content-Type header (the server can't parse the JSON body).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: HTTP = request (method/URL/headers/body) + response (status/headers/body). Verbs: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE. Codes: 2xx ok, 4xx client, 5xx server. Body is JSON.

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Define HTTP Basics for Rails APIs simply, show a small example, and mention the main trade-off or edge case.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Methods: GET (read), POST (create), PATCH (update, partial), DELETE (remove).
Status codes: 2xx success (200/201/204), 4xx client error (401/403/404/422), 5xx server (500).
Headers carry metadata: Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer.
The body for an API is usually JSON; HTTP is stateless (token per request).

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: HTTP is request/response: a client sends a request (method + URL + headers + optional body), the server returns a response (status code + headers + body). Methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT or PATCH (update; PATCH partial), DELETE (remove). Headers carry metadata (Content-Type application json, Authorization Bearer). Status codes: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 4xx client error (400, 401, 403, 404, 422), 5xx server error (500). The body for an API is usually JSON. Stateless: each request carries what it needs (the token in the header); the server keeps no session between requests. Idempotence: GET and DELETE are safe to retry; POST is not. A common mistake is returning 200 for a create, when you should use 201, and forgetting the Content-Type header, so the server can't parse the JSON body.

sections.title: Build the mental model
sections.content:

Methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update; PATCH partial), DELETE (remove).

Headers carry metadata (Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer). Status codes: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 4xx client error (400, 401, 403, 404, 422), 5xx server error (500). The body for an API is usually JSON. Stateless: each request carries what it needs (the token in the header); the server keeps no session between requests. Idempotence: GET and DELETE are safe to retry; POST is not.

Returning 200 for a create (use 201), or forgetting the Content-Type header (the server can't parse the JSON body).

sections.title: Request/Response
sections.content:
request (method/URL/headers/body) + response (status/headers/body). Codes: 2xx ok, 4xx client, 5xx server.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[request: method+URL+headers+body] --> S[server]
  S --> Re[response: status+headers+body]
  Re --> C[2xx ok / 4xx client / 5xx server]
```

sections.title: HTTP basics
sections.content:
```ruby
# A request:
#   POST /api/posts HTTP/1.1
#   Host: api.example.com
#   Content-Type: application/json
#   Authorization: Bearer <token>
#
#   { "title": "Hello", "body": "world" }   <- JSON body

# The response:
#   HTTP/1.1 201 Created
#   Content-Type: application/json
#
#   { "id": 42, "title": "Hello" }

# Methods:      GET (read) | POST (create) | PATCH (update) | DELETE (remove)
# Status codes:
#   2xx success  -> 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content
#   4xx client   -> 400 Bad, 401 Unauth, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 422 Validation
#   5xx server   -> 500 Server Error
# Headers carry metadata: Content-Type, Authorization, Accept.
# Body for an API is usually JSON.
# Stateless: each request carries what it needs (token in the header).
# Idempotent (safe to retry): GET, DELETE, PUT. NOT idempotent: POST.
```
